ArkUI is a declarative UI framework for OpenHarmony that provides a complete system for building native applications. It supports both JavaScript/ArkTS declarative APIs and C/C++ native APIs, with a unified rendering pipeline based on the Rosen graphics backend. This document provides an overview of the framework's architecture, major systems, and codebase organization.

For information about specific subsystems:

  • Core architectural patterns and pipeline details, see Core Architecture
  • Individual component implementations, see Component Patterns
  • User interaction handling, see Interaction Systems
  • Application development guides, see Developer Guides

Purpose and Scope

ArkUI serves as the complete UI stack for OpenHarmony applications, managing:

  • UI Tree Management: Component hierarchy through FrameNode and UINode classes
  • Rendering Pipeline: Vsync-driven layout, measure, and paint phases via PipelineContext
  • Event Processing: Touch, gesture, keyboard, and focus event distribution
  • Component Library: Rich set of UI components with extensible patterns
  • Multi-Language Support: JavaScript/ArkTS declarative syntax and C/C++ native APIs
  • Graphics Integration: Backend abstraction over Rosen rendering service

Core Systems Overview

The framework is built around several interconnected core systems:

PipelineContext: The Rendering Pipeline

PipelineContext orchestrates the entire rendering cycle, driven by Vsync callbacks:

Key Methods:

  • FlushVsync(uint64_t nanoTimestamp, uint64_t frameCount) - Main Vsync entry point
  • FlushBuild() - Rebuilds dirty custom nodes
  • FlushTouchEvents() - Processes queued touch input
  • FlushDragEvents() - Handles drag operations
  • Task scheduling via AddScheduleTask() and RemoveScheduleTask()

Sources: frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp834-1012 frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.h101-213

UI Tree: Node Hierarchy

The UI tree is composed of UINode and FrameNode instances:

Key Classes:

  • UINode: Base tree node with parent/child relationships (ui_node.h1-100)
  • FrameNode: Renderable node with layout and paint capabilities (frame_node.h108-142)
  • FrameProxy: Manages lazy node creation for virtual scrolling (frame_node.cpp142-494)

Key Methods:

  • AddChild(RefPtr<UINode>) - Adds child to tree
  • RemoveChild(RefPtr<UINode>) - Removes child from tree
  • MarkDirtyNode() - Marks node for re-layout/re-render

Sources: frameworks/core/components_ng/base/frame_node.cpp496-662 frameworks/core/components_ng/base/ui_node.cpp1-100

Pattern System: Component Behavior

Each component type has an associated Pattern class that defines its behavior:

Pattern Responsibilities:

  • Lifecycle management: OnAttachToFrameNode(), OnDetachFromFrameNode(), OnModifyDone()
  • Layout algorithm creation: CreateLayoutAlgorithm()
  • Paint method creation: CreateNodePaintMethod()
  • Event handling: Component-specific event callbacks

Example Patterns:

  • TextFieldPattern - Text input behavior
  • ListPattern - Scrollable list behavior
  • SwiperPattern - Carousel/swiper behavior

Sources: frameworks/core/components_ng/base/frame_node.cpp767-791 frameworks/core/components_ng/pattern/BUILD.gn19-300

Event System: User Input Processing

Events flow from the system through multiple layers:

Event Flow:

  1. Platform input (MMI) → PipelineContext
  2. EventManager performs hit testing
  3. GestureEventHub recognizes gestures
  4. Component-specific event handlers receive callbacks

Key Classes:

  • EventManager - Coordinates event distribution
  • GestureEventHub - Gesture recognition
  • TouchEvent, MouseEvent, KeyEvent - Event data structures

Sources: frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp874-992

Layout System: Size and Position Calculation

Layout is a two-phase process:

Phases:

  1. Measure: Calculate component sizes via LayoutAlgorithm::Measure()
  2. Layout: Position children via LayoutAlgorithm::Layout()

Key Classes:

  • LayoutProperty - Stores layout configuration
  • LayoutConstraint - Min/max size constraints
  • LayoutAlgorithm - Per-component layout logic
  • GeometryNode - Computed layout dimensions

Sources: frameworks/core/components_ng/base/frame_node.cpp1-100

Render System: Graphics Output

Rendering uses the Rosen graphics backend:

Key Classes:

  • RenderContext - Abstract rendering interface
  • RosenRenderContext - Rosen-specific implementation (rosen_render_context.cpp1-400)
  • PaintProperty - Visual style properties
  • RSNode - Rosen scene graph node

Rendering Process:

  1. PaintMethod::GetContentDrawFunction() generates drawing commands
  2. Commands sent to RenderContext
  3. RosenRenderContext translates to Rosen API
  4. Rosen performs GPU rendering

Sources: frameworks/core/components_ng/render/adapter/rosen_render_context.cpp326-382

API Surfaces

ArkUI provides two primary API surfaces for different use cases:

Declarative API (JavaScript/ArkTS)

Entry Points:

  • @Component decorator - Component definition
  • Built-in component functions: Text(), Button(), List(), etc.
  • Attribute modifiers: .width(), .height(), .backgroundColor(), etc.

Implementation Chain:

  1. ArkTS code calls component function (e.g., Text("hello"))
  2. JSText::Create() in js_view_abstract.cpp processes the call
  3. ModifierWithKey in arkComponent.js124-169 applies attributes
  4. arkUINativeModule.getArkUINativeModule() bridges to native
  5. TextModelNG::Create() creates the component
  6. ViewAbstract methods configure properties
  7. FrameNode added to UI tree

Sources: frameworks/bridge/declarative_frontend/jsview/js_view_abstract.cpp1-150 frameworks/bridge/declarative_frontend/engine/arkComponent.js1-170

Native C API

Entry Points:

  • OH_ArkUI_CreateNode() - Create component
  • OH_ArkUI_SetAttribute() - Set attributes
  • OH_ArkUI_AddChild() - Build tree structure

Implementation Chain:

  1. C code calls OH_ArkUI_CreateNode(ARKUI_NODE_TEXT)
  2. node_api.cpp creates ArkUINodeHandle
  3. node_text_modifier.cpp implements attribute setters
  4. Calls through to ViewAbstract methods
  5. Same FrameNode and Pattern as declarative path

Sources: interfaces/native/native_node.h36-100 frameworks/core/interfaces/arkoala/arkoala_api.h123-139 frameworks/core/interfaces/native/node/node_common_modifier.cpp1-100

Rendering Pipeline Overview

The rendering pipeline executes on every Vsync callback in a well-defined sequence:

Pipeline Phases:

PhaseMethodPurposeCode Reference
AnimationFlushAnimation()Update animation valuespipeline_context.cpp874
InputFlushTouchEvents()Process touch/mouse eventspipeline_context.cpp880
BuildFlushDirtyNodeUpdate()Rebuild dirty custom nodespipeline_context.cpp577-628
LayoutTask scheduler flushCalculate sizes and positionspipeline_context.cpp902-909
PaintTask scheduler flushGenerate drawing commandspipeline_context.cpp902-916
Post-RenderFlushFocus(), etc.Update focus, accessibilitypipeline_context.cpp968-991

Dirty Marking and Optimization:

The framework uses dirty marking to minimize redundant work:

  • AddDirtyPropertyNode() - Property changed
  • AddDirtyCustomNode() - Custom node needs rebuild
  • AddDirtyLayoutNode() - Layout recalculation needed
  • AddDirtyRenderNode() - Repaint needed

Only marked nodes are processed in each phase, enabling efficient incremental updates.

Sources: frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp834-1012 frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp577-628 frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp383-516

Thread Model

ArkUI uses a structured multi-threading model with clear separation of concerns:

Thread Types:

  • UI Thread: Executes rendering pipeline, layout, paint, event processing
  • JS Thread: Runs JavaScript/ArkTS application code
  • Platform Thread: Handles window events and lifecycle callbacks
  • IO Thread: Performs blocking I/O operations
  • GPU Thread: Submits graphics commands to GPU

Cross-Thread Communication:

  • TaskExecutor::PostTask() - Asynchronous task dispatch
  • TaskExecutor::PostSyncTask() - Synchronous blocking call
  • Thread safety enforced via CHECK_RUN_ON(UI) assertions

Typical Flow:

  1. JS state change (JS Thread) → PostTask to UI Thread
  2. UI Thread marks node dirty → next Vsync triggers re-render
  3. User touch (Platform) → PostTask to UI Thread → event dispatch → PostTask to JS Thread for callback

Sources: frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp162-217

Configuration and Initialization

Application initialization follows this sequence:

  1. UIContentImpl Creation: Entry point for UI content (ui_content_impl.cpp413-426)
  2. AceContainer Setup: Container manages pipeline and frontend (ace_container.cpp1-100)
  3. PipelineContext Creation: Rendering pipeline initialized (pipeline_context.cpp162-217)
  4. Frontend Initialization: JavaScript engine and bridge setup
  5. Root Node Setup: SetupRootElement() creates root frame node (pipeline_context.cpp145-150)

Key Configuration:

  • Window dimensions and density
  • Resource paths and asset manager
  • Theme and localization
  • Component registration

Sources: adapter/ohos/entrance/ui_content_impl.cpp413-510 adapter/ohos/entrance/ace_container.cpp82-228 frameworks/core/pipeline_ng/pipeline_context.cpp162-240
